sanskrit: yadi vāyaṃ vihitaḥ śaṃkareṇa; dharmo 'dharmo vā nātra mamāparādhaḥ gṛhṇantv ime vidhivat pāṇim asyā; yathopajoṣaṃ vihitaiṣāṃ hi kṛṣṇā
english: If this has been ordained by Shankara, whether it be dharma or adharma, the fault is not mine. Let these men take her hand in the prescribed manner; for Kṛṣṇā has indeed been destined for them as they desire.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'bravīd bhagavān dharmarājam; adya puṇyāham uta pāṇḍaveya adya pauṣyaṃ yogam upaiti candramāḥ; pāṇiṃ kṛṣṇāyās tvaṃ gṛhāṇādya pūrvam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the blessed one spoke to Dharmarāja: 'Today is an auspicious day, O Pandaveya. Today the moon enters the Puṣya constellation. You must be the first today to take Kṛṣṇā's hand.'

sanskrit: tato rājā yajñasenaḥ saputro; janyārtha yuktaṃ bahu tat tadagryam samānayām āsa sutāṃ ca kṛṣṇām; āplāvya ratnair bahubhir vibhūṣya
english: Then King Yajñasena with his son brought together the many excellent items required for the wedding ritual, and also his daughter Kṛṣṇā, having bathed her and adorned her with numerous jewels.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve suhṛdas tatra tasya; samājagmuḥ sacivā mantriṇaś ca draṣṭuṃ vivāhaṃ paramapratītā; dvijāś ca paurāś ca yathāpradhānāḥ
english: Then all his friends, ministers, and counselors assembled there, full of great delight, to witness the wedding, along with twice-born priests and townspeople according to their rank.

sanskrit: tat tasya veśmārthijanopaśobhitaṃ; vikīrṇapadmotpalabhūṣitājiram mahārharatnaughavicitram ābabhau; divaṃ yathā nirmalatārakācitam
english: That palace of his, made beautiful by the assembled guests, with its courtyard adorned with scattered lotuses and blue water-lilies and decorated with heaps of priceless gems, shone like the sky studded with bright stars.

sanskrit: tatas tu te kauravarājaputrā; vibhūṣitāḥ kuṇḍalino yuvānaḥ mahārhavastrā varacandanokṣitāḥ; kṛtābhiṣekāḥ kṛtamaṅgalakriyāḥ
english: Then those princes of the Kuru royal line, adorned with earrings, youthful, wearing magnificent garments, anointed with fine sandalwood paste, having performed the ceremonial bath and the auspicious rites—

sanskrit: purohitenāgnisamānavarcasā; sahaiva dhaumyena yathāvidhi prabho krameṇa sarve viviśuś ca tat sado; maharṣabhā goṣṭham ivābhinandinaḥ
english: —together with the family priest Dhaumya, resplendent as fire, and in accordance with the prescribed rites, O lord, all of them entered that assembly hall in order, rejoicing like great bulls entering a cow-pen.

sanskrit: tataḥ samādhāya sa vedapārago; juhāva mantrair jvalitaṃ hutāśanam yudhiṣṭhiraṃ cāpy upanīya mantravin; niyojayām āsa sahaiva kṛṣṇayā
english: Then that master of the Vedas, having kindled the fire, offered oblations into the blazing flame with sacred mantras; and the knower of mantras, having led Yudhiṣṭhira forward, joined him together with Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ tau pragṛhītapāṇī; samānayām āsa sa vedapāragaḥ tato 'bhyanujñāya tam ājiśobhinaṃ; purohito rājagṛhād viniryayau
english: That master of the Vedas caused the two of them, with joined hands, to circumambulate the fire. Then the family priest, having given his blessing to that radiant champion, departed from the king's house.

sanskrit: krameṇa cānena narādhipātmajā; varastriyās te jagṛhus tadā karam ahany ahany uttamarūpadhāriṇo; mahārathāḥ kauravavaṃśavardhanāḥ
english: In this same manner those sons of kings, great warriors who enhanced the glory of the Kuru lineage, each assuming the most handsome form day after day, took the hand of that noble woman.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca tatrādbhutarūpam uttamaṃ; jagāda viprarṣir atītamānuṣam mahānubhāvā kila sā sumadhyamā; babhūva kanyaiva gate gate 'hani
english: And the brahmin-sage there declared this supreme marvel, surpassing human understanding: that the great-souled, slender-waisted one became a virgin again with each passing day.

sanskrit: kṛte vivāhe drupado dhanaṃ dadau; mahārathebhyo bahurūpam uttamam śataṃ rathānāṃ varahemabhūṣiṇāṃ; caturyujāṃ hemakhalīnamālinām
english: After the wedding was completed, Drupada gave manifold and excellent gifts to the great chariot warriors: a hundred chariots adorned with fine gold ornaments, drawn by four horses each, with golden bridles and garlands.

sanskrit: śataṃ gajānām abhipadmināṃ tathā; śataṃ girīṇām iva hemaśṛṅgiṇām tathaiva dāsīśatam agryayauvanaṃ; mahārhaveṣābharaṇāmbarasrajam
english: Also a hundred elephants bearing lotus emblems, resembling mountains with golden peaks; and likewise a hundred maidservants in the prime of youth, wearing costly attire, ornaments, garments, and garlands.

sanskrit: pṛthak pṛthak caiva daśāyutānvitaṃ; dhanaṃ dadau saumakir agnisākṣikam tathaiva vastrāṇi ca bhūṣaṇāni; prabhāvayuktāni mahādhanāni
english: Separately and individually, the son of Sumaka gave, with fire as witness, wealth amounting to ten thousand pieces each, along with garments and jewels of great magnificence and immense value.

sanskrit: kṛte vivāhe ca tataḥ sma pāṇḍavāḥ; prabhūtaratnām upalabhya tāṃ śriyam vijahrur indrapratimā mahābalāḥ; pure tu pāñcālanṛpasya tasya ha
english: After the wedding was completed, the mighty Pāṇḍavas, resembling Indra, having thus obtained that prosperity filled with abundant riches, rejoiced in the city of the Pāñcāla king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pāṇḍavaiḥ saha saṃyogaṃ gatasya drupadasya tu na babhūva bhayaṃ kiṃ cid devebhyo 'pi kathaṃ cana
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: For Drupada, who had now gained alliance with the Pāṇḍavas, there arose no fear whatsoever, not even from the gods.

sanskrit: kuntīm āsādya tā nāryo drupadasya mahātmanaḥ nāma saṃkīrtayantyas tāḥ pādau jagmuḥ svamūrdhabhiḥ
english: Those women of the great-souled Drupada approached Kuntī, chanting her name in praise, and touched her feet with their foreheads.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇā ca kṣaumasaṃvītā kṛtakautukamaṅgalā kṛtābhivādanā śvaśrvās tasthau prahvā kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: And Kṛṣṇā, clad in linen, having performed the auspicious wedding rituals, having paid her respects to her mother-in-law, stood with bowed head and folded hands.

sanskrit: rūpalakṣaṇasaṃpannāṃ śīlācārasamanvitām draupadīm avadat premṇā pṛthāśīrvacanaṃ snuṣām
english: Pṛthā spoke with love the words of blessing to her daughter-in-law Draupadī, who was endowed with beauty and auspicious marks, and possessed of excellent character and conduct.

sanskrit: yathendrāṇī harihaye svāhā caiva vibhāvasau rohiṇī ca yathā some damayantī yathā nale
english: 'As Indrāṇī is to Indra, as Svāhā is to Agni, as Rohiṇī is to the moon, as Damayantī was to Nala—

sanskrit: yathā vaiśravaṇe bhadrā vasiṣṭhe cāpy arundhatī yathā nārāyaṇe lakṣmīs tathā tvaṃ bhava bhartṛṣu
english: —as Bhadra is to Vaiśravaṇa, as Arundhatī is to Vasiṣṭha, as Lakṣmī is to Nārāyaṇa, so may you be to your husbands.

sanskrit: jīvasūr vīrasūr bhadre bahusaukhyasamanvitā subhagā bhogasaṃpannā yajñapatnī svanuvratā
english: May you be a mother of long-lived sons, a mother of heroes, O auspicious one, endowed with great happiness, fortunate, blessed with enjoyments, a worthy partner in sacrifices, devoted to your husband.

sanskrit: atithīn āgatān sādhūn bālān vṛddhān gurūṃs tathā pūjayantyā yathānyāyaṃ śaśvad gacchantu te samāḥ
english: May your years always pass in duly honoring guests who arrive, the virtuous, children, elders, and teachers according to what is right.

sanskrit: kurujāṅgalamukhyeṣu rāṣṭreṣu nagareṣu ca anu tvam abhiṣicyasva nṛpatiṃ dharmavatsalam
english: In the chief kingdoms and cities, foremost among which is Kurujāṅgala, may you be consecrated as queen alongside a king devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: patibhir nirjitām urvīṃ vikrameṇa mahābalaiḥ kuru brāhmaṇasāt sarvām aśvamedhe mahākratau
english: The earth conquered by valor by your mighty husbands—may you dedicate it entirely to the brahmins at the great Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: pṛthivyāṃ yāni ratnāni guṇavanti gunānvite tāny āpnuhi tvaṃ kalyāṇi sukhinī śaradāṃ śatam
english: Whatever gems of quality exist on the earth—O virtuous one, may you obtain them all, and may you live happily for a hundred autumns.'

sanskrit: yathā ca tvābhinandāmi vadhv adya kṣaumasaṃvṛtām tathā bhūyo 'bhinandiṣye sūtaputrāṃ guṇānvitām
english: 'As I welcome you today, O daughter-in-law, clad in linen, so shall I again welcome you, a virtuous mother of sons, adorned with excellence.'

sanskrit: tatas tu kṛtadārebhyaḥ pāṇḍubhyaḥ prāhiṇod dhariḥ muktāvaiḍūryacitrāṇi haimāny ābharaṇāni ca
english: Then Hari sent to the sons of Pāṇḍu, now that they had taken their wife, golden ornaments adorned with pearls and vaidurya gems,

sanskrit: vāsāṃsi ca mahārhāṇi nānādeśyāni mādhavaḥ kambalājinaratnāni sparśavanti śubhāni ca
english: and Mādhava sent also the most costly garments from many lands, fine woolen blankets, precious skins, pleasant to the touch and auspicious.

sanskrit: śayanāsanayānāni vividhāni mahānti ca vaiḍūryavajracitrāṇi śataśo bhājanāni ca
english: And various large couches, seats, and conveyances, decorated with vaidurya and diamond ornaments, and hundreds of vessels—

sanskrit: rūpayauvanadākṣiṇyair upetāś ca svalaṃkṛtāḥ preṣyāḥ saṃpradadau kṛṣṇo nānādeśyāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: —and maidservants endowed with beauty, youth, and skill, well adorned, Kṛṣṇa gave by the thousands, from many different lands.

sanskrit: gajān vinītān bhadrāṃś ca sadaśvāṃś ca svalaṃkṛtān rathāṃś ca dāntān sauvarṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ paṭṭair alaṃkṛtān
english: And trained and auspicious elephants, well-caparisoned fine horses, and tamed chariots decorated with auspicious golden banners—

sanskrit: koṭiśaś ca suvarṇaṃ sa teṣām akṛtakaṃ tathā vītīkṛtam ameyātmā prāhiṇon madhusūdanaḥ
english: —and gold by the tens of millions in its raw and refined forms: the immeasurable-souled Madhusūdana sent all of this to them.

sanskrit: tat sarvaṃ pratijagrāha dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ mudā paramayā yukto govindapriyakāmyayā
english: All of this King Yudhiṣṭhira received, filled with supreme joy, out of his desire to please Govinda.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājñāṃ carair āptaiś cāraḥ samupanīyata pāṇḍavair upasaṃpannā draupadī patibhiḥ śubhā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the news was brought to the kings by their trusted spies: that the auspicious Draupadī had been won by the Pāṇḍavas and united with her husbands.

sanskrit: yena tad dhanur āyamya lakṣyaṃ viddhaṃ mahātmanā so 'rjuno jayatāṃ śreṣṭho mahābāṇadhanurdharaḥ
english: That great-souled one who, drawing that bow, had hit the target—he was Arjuna, the best among the victorious, the greatest bearer of arrows and bow.

sanskrit: yaḥ śalyaṃ madrarājānam utkṣipyābhrāmayad balī trāsayaṃś cāpi saṃkruddho vṛkṣeṇa puruṣān raṇe
english: And that mighty one who had lifted Śalya the king of Madra and whirled him about, and who in fury had terrified men in battle with a tree—

sanskrit: na cāpi saṃbhramaḥ kaś cid āsīt tatra mahātmanaḥ sa bhīmo bhīmasaṃsparśaḥ śatrusenāṅgapātanaḥ
english: —and there had been no confusion whatsoever in that great-souled one: he was Bhīma, terrible to touch, the destroyer of enemy armies.

sanskrit: brahmarūpadharāñ śrutvā pāṇḍurājasutāṃs tadā kaunteyān manujendrāṇāṃ vismayaḥ samajāyata
english: Hearing that the sons of Pāṇḍu's king, the sons of Kuntī, had been disguised in brahmin form, amazement arose among the lords of men.

sanskrit: saputrā hi purā kuntī dagdhā jatugṛhe śrutā punarjātān iti smaitān manyante sarvapārthivāḥ
english: For Kuntī along with her sons had formerly been reported burned in the house of lac. 'They have been reborn,' thought all the kings with wonder.

sanskrit: dhik kurvantas tadā bhīṣmaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca kauravam karmaṇā sunṛśaṃsena purocanakṛtena vai
english: Uttering curses then upon Bhīṣma and Dhṛtarāṣṭra the Kaurava for the most cruel deed done by Purocana—

sanskrit: vṛtte svayaṃvare caiva rājānaḥ sarva eva te yathāgataṃ viprajagmur viditvā pāṇḍavān vṛtān
english: —after the svayamvara was over, all those kings departed the way they had come, having learned that the Pāṇḍavas had been chosen.

sanskrit: atha duryodhano rājā vimanā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha aśvatthāmnā mātulena karṇena ca kṛpeṇa ca
english: Then King Duryodhana, downcast in spirit, along with his brothers, with Aśvatthāman, with his maternal uncle, with Karṇa, and with Kṛpa—

sanskrit: vinivṛtto vṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā draupadyā śvetavāhanam taṃ tu duḥśāsano vrīḍan mandaṃ mandam ivābravīt
english: —having turned back, seeing Arjuna of the white horses chosen by Draupadī, Duḥśāsana, full of shame, spoke to him slowly and haltingly:

sanskrit: yady asau brāhmaṇo na syād vindeta draupadīṃ na saḥ na hi taṃ tattvato rājan veda kaś cid dhanaṃjayam
english: 'Had he not been disguised as a brahmin, he would not have won Draupadī. For truly, O king, no one recognized Dhanañjaya for who he really was.'

sanskrit: daivaṃ tu paramaṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam dhig asmatpauruṣaṃ tāta yad dharantīha pāṇḍavāḥ
english: 'I believe fate is supreme and human effort is futile. Shame on our prowess, dear friend, seeing how the Pāṇḍavas flourish here.'

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇās te nindantaś ca purocanam viviśur hāstinapuraṃ dīnā vigatacetasaḥ
english: Speaking thus and cursing Purocana, they entered Hāstinapura, wretched and dispirited.

sanskrit: trastā vigatasaṃkalpā dṛṣṭvā pārthān mahaujasaḥ muktān havyavahāc cainān saṃyuktān drupadena ca
english: Frightened, their resolve gone, having seen the sons of Pṛthā of great power, having seen that they had escaped from the fire and were now allied with Drupada—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca saṃcintya tathaiva ca śikhaṇḍinam drupadasyātmajāṃś cānyān sarvayuddhaviśāradān
english: —and reflecting on Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍī and the other sons of Drupada, all skilled in every kind of warfare—

sanskrit: viduras tv atha tāñ śrutvā draupadyā pāṇḍavān vṛtān vrīḍitān dhārtarāṣṭrāṃś ca bhagnadarpān upāgatān
english: Then Vidura, hearing that the Pāṇḍavas had been chosen by Draupadī and that the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra had returned ashamed and broken in pride—

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanāḥ kṣattā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ viśāṃ pate uvāca diṣṭyā kuravo vardhanta iti vismitaḥ
english: —then the delighted Kṣattā, full of wonder, spoke to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O lord of the people: 'By good fortune, the Kurus prosper!'

sanskrit: vaicitravīryas tu nṛpo niśamya vidurasya tat abravīt paramaprīto diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti bhārata
english: And the son of Vichitraveerya, the king, hearing that from Vidura, spoke with supreme delight: 'By good fortune! By good fortune!' — O Bhārata.

sanskrit: manyate hi vṛtaṃ putraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ drupadakanyayā duryodhanam avijñānāt prajñācakṣur nareśvaraḥ
english: For the king whose eyes are wisdom, through ignorance believes it is his eldest son Duryodhana who has been chosen by the daughter of Drupada.

sanskrit: atha tv ājñāpayām āsa draupadyā bhūṣaṇaṃ bahu ānīyatāṃ vai kṛṣṇeti putraṃ duryodhanaṃ tadā
english: Then he commanded his son Duryodhana: 'Let the many ornaments of Draupadī be brought here — bring Kṛṣṇā!'

sanskrit: athāsya paścād vidura ācakhyau pāṇḍavān vṛtān sarvān kuśalino vīrān pūjitān drupadena ca teṣāṃ saṃbandhinaś cānyān bahūn balasamanvitān
english: But then afterward Vidura explained to him that the Pāṇḍavas had been chosen, that all the heroes were well and had been honored by Drupada, and also that they had many other powerful relatives.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yathaiva pāṇḍoḥ putrās te tathaivābhyadhikā mama seyam abhyadhikā prītir vṛddhir vidura me matā yat te kuśalino vīrā mitravantaś ca pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'Just as Pāṇḍu's sons are mine as well, so too this is greater cause for delight; this growth is greater in my view, O Vidura — that those heroic Pāṇḍavas are well and have gained allies.'

sanskrit: ko hi drupadam āsādya mitraṃ kṣattaḥ sabāndhavam na bubhūṣed bhavenārthī gataśrīr api pārthivaḥ
english: 'For who, O Kṣattā, having gained Drupada as an ally together with his kinsmen, would not prosper? Even a king who had lost his fortune and was in need would flourish.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ tathā bhāṣamāṇaṃ tu viduraḥ pratyabhāṣata nityaṃ bhavatu te buddhir eṣā rājañ śataṃ samāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Vidura replied to him who spoke thus: 'May this wisdom of yours remain firm, O king, for a hundred years.'

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaś caiva rādheyaś ca viśāṃ pate dhṛtarāṣṭram upāgamya vaco 'brūtām idaṃ tadā
english: Then Duryodhana and the son of Rādhā, O lord of the people, approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra and spoke these words to him at that time:

sanskrit: saṃnidhau vidurasya tvāṃ vaktuṃ nṛpa na śaknuvaḥ viviktam iti vakṣyāvaḥ kiṃ tavedaṃ cikīrṣitam
english: 'In Vidura's presence, O king, we are unable to speak to you. We wish to speak to you in private. What is your intention in this matter?'

sanskrit: sapatnavṛddhiṃ yat tāta manyase vṛddhim ātmanaḥ abhiṣṭauṣi ca yat kṣattuḥ samīpe dvipadāṃ vara
english: 'O dear father, best among men, you consider the growth of your enemies to be your own growth, and you praise it in Kṣattā's presence.

sanskrit: anyasmin nṛpa kartavye tvam anyat kuruṣe 'nagha teṣāṃ balavighāto hi kartavyas tāta nityaśaḥ
english: 'When one course of action is called for, O blameless king, you do another. The undermining of their strength is what must always be done, dear father.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ prāptakālasya cikīrṣāṃ mantrayāmahe yathā no na graseyus te saputrabalabāndhavān
english: 'We should deliberate upon and plan a timely course of action so that they may not devour us along with our sons, armies, and kinsmen.'

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aham apy evam evaitac cintayāmi yathā yuvām vivektuṃ nāham icchāmi tv ākāraṃ viduraṃ prati
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: 'I too think about this in the very same way as you two. But I do not wish to betray my intentions in my manner before Vidura.

sanskrit: atas teṣāṃ guṇān eva kīrtayāmi viśeṣataḥ nāvabudhyeta viduro mamābhiprāyam iṅgitaiḥ
english: 'That is why I praise their virtues specifically — so that Vidura would not understand my true intentions from my gestures and signs.

sanskrit: yac ca tvaṃ manyase prāptaṃ tad brūhi tvaṃ suyodhana rādheya manyase tvaṃ ca yat prāptaṃ tad bravīhi me
english: 'What you consider the right course of action — speak it, O Suyodhana. And you too, O son of Rādhā, tell me what you consider the right course of action.'

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca adya tān kuśalair vipraiḥ sukṛtair āptakāribhiḥ kuntīputrān bhedayāmo mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Duryodhana said: 'Today let us sow division among the sons of Kuntī and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, through skilled brahmins — trustworthy men who carry out their tasks well.

sanskrit: atha vā drupado rājā mahadbhir vittasaṃcayaiḥ putrāś cāsya pralobhyantām amātyāś caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: 'Or else King Drupada along with great hoards of wealth — and his sons and all his ministers — should be tempted and won over.

sanskrit: parityajadhvaṃ rājānaṃ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram atha tatraiva vā teṣāṃ nivāsaṃ rocayantu te
english: 'Let them be persuaded to abandon King Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī, or alternatively, let those men encourage the Pāṇḍavas to remain there itself.

sanskrit: ihaiṣāṃ doṣavad vāsaṃ varṇayantu pṛthak pṛthak te bhidyamānās tatraiva manaḥ kurvantu pāṇḍavāḥ
english: 'Let them describe, each separately, the faults and disadvantages of living here, so that the Pāṇḍavas, being divided, may set their minds on remaining there only.

sanskrit: athavā kuśalāḥ ke cid upāyanipuṇā narāḥ itaretarataḥ pārthān bhedayantv anurāgataḥ
english: 'Or else let some skillful men, expert in the use of gifts, sow discord among the sons of Pṛthā from one to another by exploiting their mutual affections.

sanskrit: vyutthāpayantu vā kṛṣṇāṃ bahutvāt sukaraṃ hi tat athavā pāṇḍavāṃs tasyāṃ bhedayantu tataś ca tām
english: 'Or let them turn Kṛṣṇā against them — that is easy given the plurality of husbands. Or alternatively let them create dissension between the Pāṇḍavas regarding her, and through her, divide them.

sanskrit: bhīmasenasya vā rājann upāyakuśalair naraiḥ mṛtyur vidhīyatāṃ channaiḥ sa hi teṣāṃ balādhikaḥ
english: 'Or, O king, let the death of Bhīmasena be arranged through men skilled in stratagems, working in secret — for he is the greatest in strength among them.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate rājan hatotsāhā hataujasaḥ yatiṣyante na rājyāya sa hi teṣāṃ vyapāśrayaḥ
english: 'For when he has been slain, O king, their enthusiasm will be crushed, their energy broken — they will no longer strive for the kingdom. He is indeed their chief support.

sanskrit: ajeyo hy arjunaḥ saṃkhye pṛṣṭhagope vṛkodare tam ṛte phalguno yuddhe rādheyasya na pādabhāk
english: 'For Arjuna is invincible in battle when Vṛkodara is guarding his back. Without Phalguna, in battle Rādheya does not even reach his feet.

sanskrit: te jānamānā daurbalyaṃ bhīmasenam ṛte mahat asmān balavato jñātvā naśiṣyanty abalīyasaḥ
english: 'Knowing their great weakness without Bhīmasena, and knowing us to be the stronger party, they who are weaker will not prevail against us.

sanskrit: ihāgateṣu pārtheṣu nideśavaśavartiṣu pravartiṣyāmahe rājan yathāśraddhaṃ nibarhaṇe
english: 'When the sons of Pṛthā have come here and are subject to our authority, O king, we shall proceed as we see fit to crush them.

sanskrit: athavā darśanīyābhiḥ pramadābhir vilobhyatām ekaikas tatra kaunteyas tataḥ kṛṣṇā virajyatām
english: 'Or alternatively let each son of Kuntī there be seduced by beautiful women, and then let Kṛṣṇā become disillusioned with them.

sanskrit: preṣyatāṃ vāpi rādheyas teṣām āgamanāya vai te loptrahāraiḥ saṃdhāya vadhyantām āptakāribhiḥ
english: 'Or let the son of Rādhā be sent to bring them here; and then, once they have been lured in with bribes, let them be slain by trusted agents.

sanskrit: eteṣām abhyupāyānāṃ yas te nirdoṣavān mataḥ tasya prayogam ātiṣṭha purā kālo 'tivartate
english: 'Of all these strategies, whichever you consider to be free of fault — proceed to employ it. The time is passing; do not delay.'
